'''Inés Margarita González Árraga''' (31 January 1973) is a Venezuelan former political prisoner, currently living in exile.<ref name=mundo>{{cite web|url=http://www.elmundo.es/cronica/2016/03/12/56daa35822601d09408b4628.html|title= Presas de Maduro|access-date=17 November 2017|date=12 March 2016|publisher=[[El Mundo (España)|El Mundo]]|language=es-ES}}</ref><ref name=prodavinci>{{cite web|url=http://prodavinci.com/2015/07/17/actualidad/perfil-quien-es-inesitaterrible-por-julett-pineda/|title=¿Quién es @inesitaterrible?|access-date=17 November 2017|last=Pineda|first= Julett|date=17 July 2015|publisher= Prodavinci|language=es-ES}}</ref>

==Biography==
González studied chemistry at the [[University of Zulia]], later completing a master's degree at the [[Venezuelan Institute for Scientific Research]] and a [[PhD]] at the [[University of Akron]] in the United States.<ref name=prodavinci/><ref name=momento>{{cite web|url= http://atodomomento.com/nacionales/ella-es-inesitalaterrible-presa-por-pensar-distinto/|title= Conoce la historia de @Inesitalaterrible, presa por pensar distinto |access-date=17 November 2017|date=17 August 2015|publisher=atodomomento.com|language=es-ES}}</ref>

On 4 October 2014, she was detained by [[Bolivarian Intelligence Service]] (SEBIN) officers for posting messages on [[Twitter]] about the death of ruling party deputy [[Robert Serra]]. She was initially indicted on charges of instigating hatred, violent insult and insulting a public official.<ref name=prodavinci/><ref name=momento/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diariolasamericas.com/maduro-encarcela-tuiteros-mensajes-politicos-n2811334|title= Maduro encarcela a tuiteros por mensajes políticos|access-date=17 November 2017|date=26 November 2014|publisher=[[Diario Las Américas]]|language=es-ES}}</ref> Her lawyer argued that this could not be an instance of violent insult, because in order to commit the offense she would have had to be in presence of the official, whereas her tweets were posted when Serra was already dead.<ref name=momento/> Subsequently, the charges of violent insult and insulting a public official were withdrawn by the Venezuelan authorities.<ref name=prodavinci/>

González was held in [[El Helicoide]], headquarters of the SEBIN in [[Caracas]], until 16 November 2015, when she was granted the humanitarian measure of house arrest by the Criminal Chamber of the [[Supreme Tribunal of Justice (Venezuela)|Supreme Tribunal of Justice]] after being diagnosed with a parauterine tumor.<ref name=mundo/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lapatilla.com/site/2015/11/17/las-primeras-palabras-de-inesita-terrible-luego-de-salir-del-helicoide/|title= Las primeras palabras de "Inesita Terrible" luego de salir del Helicoide|access-date=17 November 2017|date=17 November 2015|publisher= La Patilla|language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.el-nacional.com/noticias/historico/pronunciamiento-quotinesita-terriblequot-luego-ser-liberada_39656|title= El pronunciamiento de "Inesita Terrible" luego de ser liberada|access-date=17 November 2017|date=17 November 2015|publisher=[[El Nacional (Venezuela)|El Nacional]]|language=es-ES}}</ref>

On 27 September 2017 González fled Venezuela, saying that government officials wanted to jail her again. She currently resides in Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://elcooperante.com/la-tuitera-inesita-la-terrible-huyo-del-pais-habria-llegado-a-miami/|title=La tuitera "Inesita la terrible" huyó del país: Habría llegado a Miami|access-date=17 November 2017|date=28 September 2017|publisher=El Cooperante|language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://elcooperante.com/sabre-lo-que-es-al-fin-la-libertad-inesita-terrible-llego-a-espana-fotos/|title="Sabré lo que es al fin la libertad": Inesita Terrible llegó a España (+Fotos)|access-date=17 November 2017|date=7 October 2017|publisher=El Cooperante|language=es-ES}}</ref>
